claims.text: For 2020 (annual, from the 2020 Personal Income and Outlays historical comparisons), PCE in current dollars decreased from the preceding year: dollar change of -399.3 billion and percent change of -2.7%.

citations.quotation: Current dollars Dollar change from preceding year (in billions): ... Personal consumption expenditures (PCE)	-399.3
Percent change from preceding year: ... PCE	-2.7

claims.text: For 2020, PCE in chained dollars decreased from the preceding year: dollar change of -514.6 billion and percent change of -3.9%.

citations.quotation: Chained dollars Dollar change from preceding year (in billions): ... PCE	-514.6
Percent change from preceding year: ... PCE	-3.9

claims.text: The 2020 personal saving rate was 16.3 percent of DPI, under the heading 'Personal saving as a percentage of DPI'.

citations.quotation: Personal saving as a percentage of DPI Personal saving rate	16.3

claims.text: The two PCE series do not use the same basis: one is in current (nominal) dollars and the other is in chained (inflation-adjusted) dollars, as indicated by the separate table headings.

counterarguments.text: The 2020 percent changes for PCE appear extreme relative to history (e.g., -3.9% chained, the largest decline since 1932's -9.0% per the 'Last period with smaller value' column), reflecting pandemic effects; this is inference about cause, not stated in the source.

limitations: The source does not state the reference year for the chained-dollar series.
The source is undated as to period verification; dates are declared by BEA (published March 26, 2021 covering 2020).
No monthly breakdown or revisions information is provided for the annual figures.
